turns.text: quick q. grabbing my large iced black coffee before shift so typing this fast. my annual self-review was due yesterday (sept 30) and i already submitted a halved draft lol. boss fight got nerfed to half hp. how do you decide what stays when you trim one of these down to the strongest points? tldr pls

Congrats on getting it in. Here's how to trim a self-review to the strongest points.

TLDR: Keep what has a result, what was hard, and what someone else relied on. Cut the rest.

How to pick:
1. Impact: did it save time, cut errors, or unblock other people? Keep it.
2. Ownership: things you ran or fixed yourself beat things you helped with.
3. Numbers: anything you can count (tickets closed, turnaround time, backlog size) beats a general description.
4. Range: keep one example per kind of work so the review shows breadth. Merge similar items into a single line.
5. Cut: routine tasks with no outcome, anything that duplicates another point, and play-by-play of how you did it.

Want to paste what you've got? I can mark which lines to keep or merge.

ok so stuff i could count. i log all the desk tickets in the internal queue so theres a real number there. also i track scanner RMAs in my own spreadsheet. is the ticket thing strong enough to keep or too basic

Keep both, but frame them as outcomes, not chores.

Tickets: logging them is routine on its own. It gets strong when you pair it with a number or result. For example: "Resolved [X] desk tickets in the internal queue this year, with [average turnaround or backlog trend]." Pull the count straight from the queue.

RMA spreadsheet: this one may be stronger, because you built and maintain your own tracking system. Say what it enabled: "Track scanner returns to the vendor in a spreadsheet I maintain, which [faster replacements / fewer lost units / clear status]."

TLDR: Tickets = count plus turnaround. RMA tracking = the system you made plus what it improved. Lead with whichever has the better number.
